our_title: orderLoad() overwrites the ordering size with the file count and never range-checks ranks
ran: repro/GRA-03: `gotst p4.grf bad_count.ord /dev/null` -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 ... #0 _SCOTCHintLoad common_integer.c:129 #1 _SCOTCHorderLoad order_io.c:107'; bad_range.ord/bad_neg.ord -> 'heap-buffer-overflow WRITE ... #0 _SCOTCHorderPeri order.c:170 #1 _SCOTCHorderLoad order_io.c:120'; bad_dup.ord -> 'SEGV on unknown address ... #0 _SCOTCHorderPeri order.c:170 #1 SCOTCH_graphOrderLoad library_graph_order.c:151'; bad_short.ord (count 3 on 4 vertices) -> 'orderCheck: invalid vertex count' (ordeptr->vnodnbr silently changed). Fuzz (fuzz/tools/mutfuzz_ord.py, 1500 mutants over 5 seeds, seed 42): pristine 248 sanitizer hits in 10 buckets (intLoad overflow write, orderPeri write); patched 78 hits, all 'common_integer.c:121:15: runtime error: signed integer overflow' in intLoad (parse overflow, common_integer.c, G07). Patched: the four bad files rejected with 'orderLoad: bad input (1)' / 'invalid permutation value' / 'duplicate permutation value', check_scotch_graph_order (with the new load cases) rc=0 on 32-bit and 64-bit.
severity_note: User-controlled .ord file loaded by the public SCOTCH_graphOrderLoad() and gotst: heap writes at a file-chosen offset.
evidence: order_io.c:96 'if (intLoad (stream, &ordeptr->vnodnbr) != 1) {' after :91 'permtab = memAlloc (ordeptr->vnodnbr * sizeof (Gnum))'; :103 'for (vertnum = 0; vertnum < ordeptr->vnodnbr; vertnum ++)'; :107 'intLoad (stream, &permtab[vertnum])'; :120 'orderPeri (permtab, ordeptr->baseval, ordeptr->vnodnbr, ordeptr->peritab, ordeptr->baseval)'; order.c:170 'peritab[permtab[permnum] - permbas] = permnum + peribas;' with no check.
review_accuracy: Accurate. It misses the duplicate-rank case (holes in peritab, later SEGV) and the fact that a smaller count silently changes ordeptr->vnodnbr.
first_pass_critique: Status, evidence and preferred option are right. Its sketch kept the now-useless `permtab` allocation and `memFree` calls (the committed patch removes the temporary array altogether, as building the inverse on the fly makes it dead) and did not add the natural regression test to test_scotch_graph_order.c (which had a save step but no load step).

our_title: hgraphOrderCp()/hmeshOrderCp() leak the coarse column block tree and mutex on strategy failure
ran: repro/GRA-25/leak (stack-scrubbing harness, LSan on, 1 thread): graph `c{rat=0.9,cpr=o{strat=b{cmin=0,strat=s}},unc=s}` on dbl2.grf -> 'Direct leak of 56 byte(s) ... #1 _SCOTCHhgraphOrderCc #2 _SCOTCHhgraphOrderSt #3 _SCOTCHhgraphOrderCp'; mesh `c{rat=0.9,cpr=n{sep=h,ole=b{cmin=0,strat=s},ose=s},unc=s}` on dbl.msh -> 'Direct leak of 72 byte(s) ... #1 _SCOTCHhmeshOrderNd #2 _SCOTCHhmeshOrderSt #3 _SCOTCHhmeshOrderCp'. Patched: 'order ret=1', no leak, both. check_prog_gord/mord rc=0 32/64-bit.
severity_note: Only on strategy failure; leak plus an undestroyed mutex.
evidence: hgraph_order_cp.c:449-454 'if (hgraphOrderSt (&coargrafdat, &coarordedat, 0, &coarordedat.rootdat, paraptr->stratcpr) != 0) { memFree (coarperitab); hgraphExit (&coargrafdat); memFree (finecoartax + ...); return (1); }' (no orderExit); success path :496 'orderExit (&coarordedat);'. hmesh_order_cp.c:386-389 same without orderExit.
upstream_change: 6a00c51 touched hgraph_order_cp.c for unsigned bit sets only
review_accuracy: Accurate; the mesh twin hmeshOrderCp() has the same defect (not mentioned).
first_pass_critique: Right fix for the graph side; it noted the mesh twin as 'not checked' and did not patch it. Its gord-based evidence is polluted by hgraphOrderNd error-path leaks; the committed repro isolates the Cp leak. While verifying, the orderExit() call exposed PS2-G15-1 (hgraphOrderCc leaves uninitialized tree cells), fixed in 0004.

fix_options.label: a. orderExit() on the error path of both Cp routines (committed)
fix_options.summary: Free the partial tree and destroy the mutex with orderExit(&coarordedat) before freeing the compressed structure.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Requires every tree-building strategy to leave a consistent tree on failure (hgraphOrderCc did not: 0004).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same call as his success path (hgraph_order_cp.c:496, hmesh_order_cp.c:434), reverse order of acquisition.

fix_options.label: b. Make each tree-building strategy free its own partial tree on failure
fix_options.summary: hgraphOrderNd/hgraphOrderCc/hmeshOrderNd free cblktab on error so that no tree is left behind.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Three sites instead of two, sub-trees of already-ordered children still leak unless recursive; the coarse ordering mutex still needs orderExit().
fix_options.maintainer_fit: More invasive; the Order object owns its tree and orderExit() is the designed destructor.

notes: No src/check home: the leak only shows with LSan on a deliberately failing strategy. hgraphOrderNd2 error path leaks its induced subgraphs (seen in the same LSan runs, PS2-G15-8, not patched).

our_title: Block ordering splits in vertex order, re-runs its strategy per sub-block, and drops trailing zero-load columns
ran: repro/GRA-22/bl (20x20 grid, loads 1+i, SCOTCH_graphOrderCompute + SCOTCH_graphOrderCheck, block weights through peritab): pristine `b{cmin=1200,strat=g}` -> 'min=24 max=16930', 5 blocks heavier than 2cmin+maxload; patched 'min=954 max=1577', 0. Loads 1+((i*7919)%23), `b{cmin=100,strat=g}`: pristine min=66 max=139, patched min=88 max=118. ND leaves `n{...,ole=b{cmin=1200,strat=g},ose=b{cmin=1200,strat=g}}` loads 1+i: pristine min=233 max=2713, patched min=162 max=2235. Zero loads (`b{cmin=1,strat=s}` on 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0): pristine 'covered=6/8 rang_end=6' and SCOTCH_graphOrderCheck=1; patched 'covered=8/8' check=0. `b{cmin=100,strat=n{sep=m{...},ole=s,ose=s}}`: pristine timeout 10 s (rc=124), patched 207 blocks check=0. Mesh twin: `mord dbl.msh '-ob{cmin=2,strat=n{sep=h,ole=s,ose=s}}'` pristine rc=124, patched rc=0. Same with bl64. check_prog_gord (incl. m16x16_b100000_v.grf with ole=b/ose=b), check_prog_gord_block, check_prog_gotst, check_prog_mord rc=0 32/64-bit.
severity_note: Higher than the review's 'low': silent wrong result on every weighted use of 'b' (documented semantics violated), plus a hang for 'b{strat=<tree-building strategy>}' and an inconsistent tree with zero loads.
evidence: hgraph_order_bl.c:140 'vnodnum = grafptr->s.baseval;' and :162 'vnlosum += grafptr->s.velotax[vnodnum];' (local vertex order) while :167 'cblkptr->cblktab[cblknum].vnodnbr = vnodnum - vnodbas;' is applied to ordering positions; :172 'while (vnlosum < grafptr->vnlosum)' stops before trailing zero-weight columns; :192 'if (hgraphOrderBl (grafptr, ordeptr, ordenum, cblkptr->cblktab + cblknum, paraptr) != 0)' re-enters :96 'hgraphOrderSt (grafptr, ...)' on the whole graph for each sub-block; s_l.tex:1357-1360 'the resulting separators tree is traversed and all of the column blocks that are larger than 2 size are split ... without changing the ordering that has been computed'.
upstream_change: a90b1cb (7.0.11) 'Bugfix: do not get vertex loads through inverse permutation' replaced velotax[peritab[vnodnum]] (which indexed the local load array with original vertex numbers on induced subgraphs) by velotax[vnodnum]; 7.0.17 untouched.
review_accuracy: The defect is real but its 'Fix:' (go back through peritab) is exactly what a90b1cb removed because it is out of bounds on induced subgraphs (ND leaves, 'o' components, partial orderings); it also missed the non-terminating recursion and the zero-load case.
first_pass_critique: Correct diagnosis (including the recursion, its NEW-1) and a structurally right rewrite, but its load array is indexed in original-vertex space and allocated with ordeptr->vnodnbr (the whole graph) at every call, i.e. O(N) memory per nested dissection leaf; it also kept the whole-graph vnlosum/vnohnbr on the recursion. The committed patch builds the column loads in ordering order with two O(n log n) sorts of (original index, value) pairs for induced subgraphs (direct access for the original graph), splits leaves recursively with per-block offsets, handles trailing zero loads, and fixes the mesh twin's recursion.

fix_options.label: a. Run strategy once, compute column loads in ordering order, split leaves recursively (committed)
fix_options.summary: hgraphOrderBl() runs the strategy, builds vnlotab (loads indexed by ordering number; via peritab for original graphs, by sorting (vnumtax, velotax) and (peritab, position) pairs with intSort2asc1 for induced subgraphs), then static hgraphOrderBl2() walks the tree with the ordering offset of each sub-block and splits leaves; trailing zero-weight columns go to the last block; a split yielding one block is undone. hmeshOrderBl() gets the same split between strategy and static hmeshOrderBl2().
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two temporary arrays (n and 4n Gnums) on weighted induced subgraphs; block boundaries change for weighted graphs (intended); SEQU nodes with a single child are no longer produced.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Static '2' helper declared in the .h under the file marker (his hgraph_order_cp.h:95-97 idiom); intSort2asc1 pair matching as in mapLoad (mapping_io.c:158); behaviour is the one his manual documents.

fix_options.summary: Restore velotax[peritab[...]] when vnumtax == NULL, keep vertex order for induced subgraphs; does not fix the recursion nor zero loads.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Leaves ND leaves (the main use of 'b', e.g. check_prog_gord's ole=b) unbalanced and the hang in place.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Not a fix of the documented semantics; he already rejected the peritab indexing in a90b1cb.

our_title: graphCoarsen2() ignores the threads' error status and returns 0 with a freed or unfilled coarse graph
ran: repro/GRA-14 (LD_PRELOAD injector inj.so failing the N-th allocation, ASAN_OPTIONS=verify_asan_link_order=0:detect_leaks=1, SCOTCH_graphCoarsen on bump.grf): pristine 1 thread N=7 -> 'graphCoarsen3: out of memory (1)' then 'ret=0' and 'AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... #0 _SCOTCHgraphCheck ... freed by ... graphCoarsen3'; N=8 -> 'graphCoarsen3: out of memory (2)' then 'ret=0 coarse: vertnbr=5016 edgenbr=0 check=1'; match mode N=4 -> 'graphMatch: out of memory' then 'ret=0 match: coarvertnbr=0 badmates=9800'; 4 threads: N=11 'graphMatchInit: out of memory' + LeakSanitizer (mating array), N=13-16 'graphMatch: out of memory' + leak of the lock array (graphMatchInit), N=18 use-after-free, N=19-22 'out of memory (2)' then ret=0 with 'graphCheck: invalid vertex arrays' + leaks of the other threads' hash tables. Patched: every N in 3..60 (1 thread), 10..90 (4 threads) and match mode returns 2 with LSan clean, 32-bit and 64-bit; check_scotch_graph_coarsen/map, check_prog_gpart rc=0 both trees.
severity_note: Out-of-memory only, but then callers (all multilevel methods) use a freed or uninitialized graph; agrees with the review.
evidence: graph_coarsen.c:256-258 'if (coargrafptr->verttax != NULL) memFree (coargrafptr->verttax); coarptr->retuval = 2;' (pointer left dangling); :555-556 'if (coargrafptr->verttax == NULL) return (coarptr->retuval);' then :566 'return (0);' regardless of retuval; :371 'coarptr->retuval = 2;' after a hash-table failure with the coarse arrays already allocated; :552-553 'if (coargrafptr == NULL) return (0);' reached after a graphMatch failure in graphCoarsenMatch(); :527-528 'if (graphMatchInit (coarptr, thrdnbr) != 0) return (2);' leaks finematetab; graph_match.c:322-326 frees only the thread's own queue.
review_accuracy: Accurate for the two cited cases; it missed the graphCoarsenMatch() case (returns 0 with an invalid mating array after a queue allocation failure) and the leaks on the threaded error paths.
first_pass_critique: Its diff (NULL verttax + 'retuval != 0 after verttax check') still returns 0 from graphCoarsenMatch() on a matching failure (the coargrafptr == NULL early return precedes its new test) and reads coargrafptr->verttax from an uninitialized caller structure when the failure happens before thread 0's memSet; it leaves the mating/lock/hash leaks. Its 'one of 6 multi-threaded runs hung' remark was not reproduced here (all 90 injection points at 4 threads terminate). The committed patch moves the memSet of the coarse graph before the thread launch so that graphCoarsen2() can act on retuval uniformly.
